title: Dense transformer baseline
question: What does a plain ~10M-param causal transformer reach on TinyStories at our compute budget? Every later arc is measured against this.
prediction: Written 2026-11-22 before the run. After 200M tokens of Python (code-py-v1), full-val loss lands in 0.90-1.30 nats/token (about 0.35-0.50 bits/char). Throughput about 170k tok/s compiled, about 20 min. Samples are syntactically plausible Python with coherent short functions but frequent logic errors.
notes: Run E0-20261122-122059-s0 (commit 0dc7491, seed 0, 200M tokens). Prediction check: loss range MISSED (0.606 vs predicted 0.90-1.30; the curated corpus is far more predictable than assumed). Samples: plausible Python, palindrome prompt solved with correct asserts, but fibonacci degenerated into repeated 'else:' lines.

title: Linear-time mixers
question: Can Gated DeltaNet (vs Mamba-2 vs sliding-window only) plus one global attention layer match the baseline, while memory stops growing with context?
prediction: Written 2026-11-22 before the run. Same depth, about the same params as E0, but only one full-attention layer. Val loss within +-2% of E0 and more likely slightly better (hybrids tend to win at short context; the 100-step bench was already lower: 2.58 vs 2.84). About 1.7x slower wall-clock than E0 because of the GDN kernels (100k vs 173k tok/s). If it is worse than E0 by >3%, suspect the GDN parametrisation or the SWA window.
notes: Run E1-20261122-124440-s0. Prediction check: direction right, magnitude MISSED: -3.6% vs E0 (predicted within +-2%). Led E0 at every eval checkpoint. Wall-clock 1.66x E0 (predicted ~1.7x). Best model so far, with one full-attention layer out of six.

title: Looped core block
question: Does one shared core block looped r times match a deeper unshared model with far fewer parameters? Does quality keep improving when r at test time exceeds r in training?
prediction: Written 2026-11-22 before the run. At r=4 (about 2x E0's FLOPs/token, 11% fewer non-emb params), val loss matches E0 within +-3%, so we expect no win per token yet; the claim to test is the r curve. Predicted shape: r=1 clearly worse (> +10% vs r=4); r=2 < r=1; r=4 about r=6 (flat); r=8 about the same or slightly better than r=4; r=12 (beyond the trained max of 7) flat or slightly worse, not a collapse. Training is stable (no loss spikes > 0.5 after warmup).
notes: Run E2-20261122-132340-s0. Prediction check: r=4 within 3% of E0 (+2.0%) HIT; r=1 > +10% MISSED (+8.2%); r=2 < r=1 HIT; r=4 ~ r=6 HIT (+0.9%); r=8 <= r=4 MISSED (+2.3%); r=12 no collapse HIT but worse than 'slightly' (+5.7%); stability HIT (no spikes, max grad-norm 0.67). The loss is best at r=4 (= mean training r) and degrades when extrapolating: the loops don't converge to a fixed point. At 2.1x E1's FLOPs it is 5.8% worse than E1: no win per token or per FLOP at this scale.
